books.title: Duck, Sir Hopsalot!
books.blurb: Sir Hopsalot, the grandest bunny in the park, pushes in at the Rail Race and challenges RiPika, then bonks every striped bar because he thinks “duck” means a duck, until RiPika gives up her lead to show him.
books.adversary: Sir Hopsalot, a pompous white bunny (the 'bunny' model) with the tallest ears in the park: a rival. He pushes in at the Rail Race queue, calls RiPika “small yellow person” and challenges her to a race, then bonks bar after bar because nobody ever told him that “duck” means get down low. Resolved kindly: RiPika could win easily but slows down to teach him; he ducks the last bar beside her; she wins by the tip of her nose; he keeps his promise to call her magnificent (and they argue happily about who is more magnificent); and the next day he gives her a rubber duck and queues at the back like everybody else.
jokes: p1: the boasting: tallest ears, fluffiest tail, and he never stops telling everybody about it
p3: caught pushing in, he just sniffs “Nonsense” and challenges the “small yellow person” to a race
p4: “DUCK!” / “A duck? Where?” / BONK! His ears go wibble-wobble (the running gag starts)
p5: He peered left. He peered right. He peered up. BONK! “Still no duck,” he grumbled.
p6: “Everybody keeps shouting about ducks, and there are no ducks anywhere!”
p9: an argument made entirely of compliments: “You are magnificent.” “So are you!” “No, YOU are!”
p10: the payoff, a rubber duck: “At last,” laughed RiPika, “a duck!”

books.title: The Loudest Shush
books.blurb: Trilla the singing puff cannot stop singing in the library, and grumpy Mrs Crumpet the library cat shushes louder every time, until Trilla works out that the cat is not cross at all, just sleepy.
books.adversary: Mrs Crumpet, the grumpy ginger library cat (the 'kitten' model; the game's own library cat is ginger and a she), left in charge while the owl librarian is out. A grump whose every SHHHH is louder than the singing, humming or hiccupping it is meant to stop. She turns out to have been misunderstood: she hasn't had a proper nap for three days, and nobody has sung her a lullaby since she was a kitten. Resolved when Trilla sings the softest lullaby: Mrs Crumpet falls asleep purring like a tractor, Trilla shushes her, and Trilla sings her a lullaby every nap time after.

p7: her biggest shush yet comes out as an enormous YAWN

It found what people lost and kept it safe behind the pink wall, and it could never give anything back because everyone took one look at its eyebrows and ran. books.title: Bumps in the Library
books.blurb: Something goes bump in the library every night, so you and the owl librarian hide behind the big red armchair to catch the culprit, and find a shy mouse who only wanted to read.
books.adversary: A midnight muddler who knocks books down, leaves crumbs and, worst of all, folds down page corners. The sleeping library cat is the only suspect, but she has been asleep since last Christmas and the footprints in the dust are far too small for her. A stake-out behind the big red armchair catches a shy mouse who loves stories but is too small for the shelves and too scared of the cat to come by day. The owl gives her a bookmark and the smallest library card ever, and now she reads aloud curled up on the sleeping cat.
jokes: Page 2: To a librarian, folded page corners are the naughtiest thing of all.
Page 3: The owl whispers everything because it is a library. She even whispers her sneezes.

Pages 6-7: The owl can only see in the dark with her glasses on, and she can't find them. They are on top of her head. The page 6 picture shows them there, so the reader spots them first.
Page 8: The culprit's first words to the owl who shushes everyone: 'Please don't shush me!'
Page 10: The cat sleeps through every story but purrs at the good bits.

books.title: The Giant Footprints
books.blurb: Giant footprints appear all over the park and everyone hides, until brave RiPika follows them to Grandpa Tock, a 102-year-old tortoise who has never been on a ride.
books.adversary: A 'giant' whose dinner-plate footprints circle the fountain, nibble every yellow flower and creep towards the rides, until the whole park is hiding. RiPika works out from the close-together prints that it walks very slowly, so it can't be scary. She follows the trail to Grandpa Tock, the 102-year-old tortoise, who sets off for the Rail Race every evening but is so slow that the carts are asleep when he arrives. RiPika calls the cat bus to carry him, everyone who hid from him comes out to wave, and he finally gets his ride.
